items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: I am really never inclined to estimate a musician by his life, but only by his music. And what I hear is all I know.

ctx.x: Well, you wouldn't be able to hear that in his horn. And you would have to know something about his life then. However, it seemed to me that he was constantly, he spent most of his life in search of approval. And he looked for the applause and he gloried in the response. He was not a congenital hermit by any means. And so, however, I am really never inclined to estimate a musician by his life, but only by his music. And what I hear is all I know.

Now, it's been said that, and I think Frank Power said this in a tape that he did in Bidebeck's life, that there was only one other musician that bare any resemblance to Bix Bidebeck. In the sense that both these musicians were victimized by the changing values of their time. And he mentions Charlie Parker. Now, I don't want to talk about, I don't want to bring up Charlie Parker. I'd rather talk about Bix Bidebeck. But, it's very interesting to me that he should bring up Charlie Parker in the relationship to Bix…

Well, it may have dramatized it to some extent, but I believe that the decline of the actualities behind the dream had already begun sometime earlier than that. I believe firmly that the American system has been in decline, demonstrably in decline, since the beginning of World War I. As far as the application of Charlie Parker, of course, I knew Charlie Parker and I didn't know Big Spider-Bank. However, it's fair to say that I know more about Big Spider-Bank than I know about Charlie Parker. In the first place,…
